newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Kerry Group confident of good result in '97.
newsitem.headline: Kerry Group confident of good result in '97.

text.p: Irish food company Kerry Group Plc said on Tuesday that the restructuring and integration programmes in its food ingredients and consumer foods businesses was complete and it was confident of another good result in the current year.
Earlier, Kerry reported an 18.6 percent increase in 1996 pre-tax profits to 51.2 million punts.
Kerry said in a statement that its balance sheet was considerably strengthened as the group had reduced borrowings as planned while continuing to invest in the quality of its asset base.
We will continue to explore complementary acquisition opportunities in international growth markets in line with the groups corporate development strategy, Kerry said.

The company said that it had completed the restructuring and integration of the DCA and Margetts businesses as planned while the UK-based Mattesson Wall's chilled meats business, acquired at the end of 1994, was fully integrated with Kerry Foods.

"The completion of both integration programmes, costing a total of 15.0 million Irish pounds in the year under review, will produce substantial savings and synergies throughout our core businesses in the years ahead," Kerry said.
The group also said that specialist fruit ingredients manufacturer Ciprial, acquired in February 1996, was integrated into Kerry's fruit ingredients division.
"This has considerably strengthened Kerry's position as a leading supplier of fruit flavours and preparations to the yoghurt, ice cream, dairy and bakery industries on a European wide basis."
The company also acquired the remaining 50 percent equity of joint venture partnership Solutech DCA from Cerebos Australia last March.

"This Australian manufacturing base establishes an important foothold for the group in supplying food coatings and seasonings to the food industry in Australia and New Zealand and will spearhead the growth of Kerry Ingredients in the Asia-Pacific area."

The company said net group borrowings at year-end were 305 million Irish pounds, down from 314 million at end-1995 while the debt/equity ratio fell to 83 percent compared to 95 percent a year earlier.
The reduction in borrowings was achieved after expenditure of 56.3 million on the acquisition of Ciprial and DCA-Solutech and 34.9 million on capital projects.
Operating cashflow increased to 138.0 million from 110.3 million in 1995 while Kerry's tax charge rose to 7.1 million in 1996 from 5.1 million a year earlier.

"Accordingly, the effective tax charge has increased from 11.7 percent to 13.9 percent in line with a shift in the relative rate of profits growth between Ireland and overseas operations," Kerry said.
